intro.title: Environment & config
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js application that reads environment variables and configuration settings. You'll learn the core concept of separating configuration from code to make your app adaptable across different environments like development and production. The main technologies involved are Node.js's built-in 'process.env' object and the 'dotenv' package for managing environment variables. By the end, you'll have a configurable app that can securely handle settings like API keys and database URLs.
intro.usecase: Environment configuration is essential for any Node.js application that needs to adapt to different deployment environments like development, testing, and production. In real-world applications, this pattern appears when managing database connection strings, API keys, and service URLs that vary between environments. For example, an e-commerce dashboard might use different payment gateway credentials in production versus development, while a content management system would connect to different database instances. Developers use environment variables to securely store sensitive configuration data and ensure their applications behave correctly across all deployment stages without hardcoding values.
